metadata.title: Semita — Find your path through AI
metadata.description: A community-driven hub to compare LLMs: cost per token, context windows, benchmarks and real-world recommendations — so you can pick the right model.

footer.tagline: Semita — open source, community-driven. AI that leverages you, not replaces you.
footer.disclaimer: Prices and benchmarks are references — always verify the official source.

home.subtitle: Semita is a community-driven hub that compares LLMs by cost per token, context window, benchmarks and real-world recommendations — one clear path to the right model, without digging through a dozen sites.

features.costBody: Input and output prices side by side, so you can estimate the real spend of your use case before committing.
features.contextBody: Context windows, modalities and the real strengths of each model — explained without jargon.
features.communityBody: What each model is actually good at in practice, backed by open, verifiable sources.

home.roadmapSubtitle: Semita grows one pillar at a time — each phase ships only when the previous one is solid.

phases.chooseBody: A living LLM comparison hub: benchmarks, cost per token, strengths and community recommendations, filterable by use case.
phases.applyBody: A directory of skills and MCPs, organized and filterable by personal and professional goals, built on the same data and tag structure.
phases.learnBody: A progressive path from first prompts to local models and evaluation — starting with the beginner → advanced guide.
phases.validateBody: A truthfulness voting system for every article and entry — enabled only once there is a critical mass of active users.

guide.title: From first chat to sharp judgment
guide.subtitle: A practical path: what AI is for in your life, how to start without overwhelm, and how to level up toward local models, cost control and honest evaluation.
guide.mindsetBody: Semita treats AI as a force multiplier: it drafts, searches, explains and speeds loops — you decide what is true, what ships, and what matters. The goal is not to disappear behind a model; it is to get better outcomes with clearer ownership.
guide.mindsetBadge: Rule of thumb: if you cannot explain the result to a colleague, do not ship it yet.
guide.forWhomTitle: What is this for — for you?
guide.forWhomSubtitle: Same tools, different jobs. Pick the lane that matches your week.

student.title: Student / lifelong learner
student.body: Turn dense material into outlines, quizzes and analogies. Ask for counter-arguments. Never paste graded work you have not rewritten in your own words.

builder.title: Developer / maker
builder.body: Debug, scaffold, review diffs and explore APIs. Keep secrets out of prompts. Prefer models strong at coding — then verify with tests.

writer.title: Writer / creator
writer.body: Brainstorm angles, tighten structure, localize tone. You own voice and facts. Use AI for first passes and editing passes — not as the final byline.

lead.title: Founder / ops / lead
lead.body: Summarize options, draft SOPs, stress-test plans. Watch cost and privacy on customer data. Compare models before locking a vendor habit.

private.title: Privacy-minded user
private.body: Prefer local / open weights when the topic is sensitive. Filter Semita by local + hardware tier. Cloud APIs are fine for non-sensitive exploration.

guide.pathSubtitle: Climb only as far as your goals need. Each level assumes the one above it.

beginner.title: Get useful answers on day one
beginner.for: You have used ChatGPT-like tools a little — or not at all — and want reliable help without jargon.
beginner.tip1: State the goal, audience and constraints in one short paragraph before asking for output.
beginner.tip2: Ask for examples and a checklist, then do a small task yourself so you learn the pattern.
beginner.tip3: Treat every factual claim as a draft: verify dates, numbers and citations elsewhere.
beginner.tip4: Start with a strong general model in the catalog; specialize later when you know your use case.
beginner.tip5: Save prompts that worked. Reuse and tweak — do not reinvent the brief every time.

intermediate.title: Make AI part of a real workflow
intermediate.for: You already get decent drafts and want consistency, cost awareness and better model fit.
intermediate.tip1: Split work into roles: research → outline → draft → critique. One chat trying to do everything gets muddy.
intermediate.tip2: Compare 2–3 models on the same prompt (Semita Compare) before standardizing a stack.
intermediate.tip3: Watch context size: dump only what the task needs. Long pastes raise cost and dilute attention.
intermediate.tip4: Tag use cases (coding, writing, research, local). Match model strengths instead of chasing hype names.
intermediate.tip5: Add a verification step: tests, linters, human review, or a second model as critic.

advanced.title: Own the stack — cloud, local and judgment
advanced.for: You care about latency, privacy, spend and repeatable quality across a team or product.
advanced.tip1: Run capable local models on your hardware when data must stay offline; keep cloud for peak quality bursts.
advanced.tip2: Pin model IDs and prices when evaluating — Semita Mini Benchmark methodology shows how maintainers do that.
advanced.tip3: Build eval sets from your real tasks (10–30 examples beats a leaderboard you do not trust).
advanced.tip4: Separate quality, latency and cost in decisions. The cheapest model that fails is not cheap.
advanced.tip5: Document when AI may and may not touch customer or regulated data — tooling follows policy, not the reverse.

guide.topicsSubtitle: Short primers you can revisit whenever a new model drops.

prompts.title: Prompts that carry intent
prompts.body: Good prompts name role, goal, format, constraints and success criteria. Bad prompts ask the model to “be smart.” Prefer concrete verbs and examples of the shape you want.

context.title: Context windows
context.body: Context is working memory, not infinite wisdom. Stuffing a whole repo often hurts more than a focused file plus a clear question. Check the catalog’s context field when your task is long.

cloudLocal.title: Cloud API vs local
cloudLocal.body: Cloud: strongest models, easy updates, data leaves your machine. Local: privacy, offline, predictable cost after hardware — with VRAM/RAM limits. Semita filters help you see both.

cost.title: Cost per token (and why it matters)
cost.body: Input and output are priced differently. Long system prompts and verbose answers add up. Estimate before you automate a high-volume path — then re-check the provider page.

privacy.title: Privacy & secrets
privacy.body: Never paste API keys, passwords or personal data you are not allowed to share. For sensitive work, prefer local runtimes (Ollama, LM Studio, llama.cpp, MLX) and open weights.

eval.title: How to know it is working
eval.body: Define a tiny scorecard for your job: correctness, tone, latency, cost. Re-run the same cases when you switch models. Public leaderboards are signals — your tasks are the exam.

guide.nextBody: Use the catalog with filters for use case, local hardware and cost — then compare side by side.

score.title: Semita score methodology
score.subtitle: The Semita score is an editorial 1.0–5.0 rating for the Phase 1 MVP. It helps you scan the catalog quickly — it is not a live community vote.
score.editorial: Until Phase 4 (community validates), maintainers set each score by reading public docs, pricing and known strengths. Every score can be challenged via a data-update issue with sources.
score.scaleBody: 5.0 = exceptional fit for its intended use cases at the listed price. 4.0–4.9 = strong default pick. 3.0–3.9 = solid with clear trade-offs. Below 3.0 = niche or outdated for most Semita users.

factors.qualityBody: Public benchmarks and documented strengths for coding, writing, reasoning or multimodal work — never invented numbers.
factors.valueBody: List price per million tokens relative to peers in the same capability band.
factors.fitBody: How often the model is a sensible default for the tagged use cases, not just a leaderboard winner.
factors.trustBody: Official pricing/docs links and a recent lastUpdated date. Stale or weakly sourced entries score lower until refreshed.

score.notVotes: Not live community votes (that lands in Phase 4).
score.notBenchmark: Not a single benchmark score — those stay listed separately with sources.
score.notGuarantee: Not a purchase recommendation or SLA — always verify the official provider page.

benchmark.title: Semita Mini Benchmark
benchmark.subtitle: A small, transparent task suite run by maintainers — same prompts, pinned model IDs, snapshotted prices. Quality, latency and cost stay separate so trade-offs stay visible.
benchmark.honesty: This is not a live public runner and not a scientific leaderboard. Results are versioned in Git after a private maintainer run. Until the first official round is published, this page shows the methodology and pending state only.
benchmark.pendingBody: The suite is ready. Results will appear here after a maintainer configures AI Gateway and publishes a reviewed run — no invented demo numbers.
benchmark.pendingStep2: Run pnpm benchmark:run --max-usd 2, then complete blinded human review.
benchmark.tasksSubtitle: Ten short prompts across five categories. Full prompts are public so anyone can audit the suite.
